# Business Leaders Forum

Since 2018, France Japan Business Leaders Forum is a series of 10 thought leadership conferences, which aims at gathering industry experts on dedicated events to discuss industry trends, challenges and opportunities, as well as providing a networking platform to promote France – Japan collaboration.

Establish & develop partnerships with business actors in France and Japan, learn about sectorial and technological evolutions, exchange on the challenges and opportunities of their sector, give visibility to their structure, prospects, competitors, professional associations and governmental authorities by participating in key discussions among many themes.

Hosted by high profiles speakers, this year’s series marks the 8 th edition of the Business Leaders Forum, and all webinars and conferences will help start building the “Japanese paths towards the future”. The opening “ French Japanese Business Summit ” event will be held on December 1st, 2026 , at Nikkei Hall in Tokyo.

# Explore Exhibition Booths

# Explore Exhibition Booths

At the French-Japanese Business Summit, the Nikkei Hall will host a variety of food, beverage and partner stands . Visitors will have the chance to taste products, discover new flavors, and meet the brands behind them. It’s the perfect place to enjoy, network, and experience French-Japanese gastronomy .

## Partners

## Details

Savencia is a leading international food group specializing in cheese and dairy products . With brands like Caprice des Dieux , Saint Agur , and Bresso , the group combines innovation and tradition to offer high-quality products worldwide . Present in over 120 countries , Savencia is committed to sustainability , taste , and craftsmanship , serving both consumers and culinary professionals.

Aux Merveilleux de Fred is a French patisserie known for its delicate meringue-based cakes coated in whipped cream and chocolate shavings. Founded by Frédéric Vaucamps , the brand celebrates artisanal savoir-faire and French tradition . With boutiques across Europe , Asia , and North America , it offers a refined taste of Parisian indulgence around the world.

Godiva is a premium Belgian chocolate brand known for its artisanal expertise and rich heritage since 1926 . It offers a wide range of luxury chocolates , truffles , and gourmet treats , blending tradition with innovation . With a strong global presence , Godiva is dedicated to providing indulgent experiences through high-quality ingredients and elegant presentation .

Perrier is a French mineral water brand famous for its natural carbonation and distinctive green bottle . Sourced from Vergèze in the south of France, Perrier combines purity , refreshing taste , and a sparkling effervescence . Often associated with elegance and sophistication , Perrier is enjoyed worldwide as a premium sparkling water , both on its own and as a mixer.

# Explore Exhibition Booths

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/business-leaders-forum/business-summit-0611/explore-exhibition-stands.html
Meiji Holdings is a premier Japanese multinational headquartered in Tokyo , specializing in food , dairy , confectionery , nutrition , and pharmaceuticals . Founded in 1916/1917 , its leading subsidiaries include Meiji Co. (food and dairy) and Meiji Seika Pharma (medicine and vaccines). Meiji is known for iconic Japanese brands like Meiji Milk Chocolate , Oishii Gyunyu , and Kinoko no Yama , and it operates globally with sustainable innovation at its core.

Ile de France® is a French cheese brand inspired by the iconic ocean liner that first brought French cheese to the U.S. in 1936 . Reflecting French art de vivre , the brand offers a wide range of authentic and innovative cheeses , allowing consumers worldwide to enjoy refined snacks , enhance dishes , or create elegant cheese boards .

IWA is a premium Japanese sake brand founded by former Dom Pérignon cellar master Richard Geoffroy . Crafted in Toyama, IWA combines tradition and innovation through a unique blending approach called Assemblage , using different rice types, yeast strains, and brewing techniques. The result is a refined , complex sake that balances richness and purity . IWA redefines sake for a global audience, offering a modern expression of Japan’s iconic beverage .

Scapes is a Japanese brand that offers a contemporary reinterpretation of the traditional art of bonsai, combining natural elements with industrial materials such as stainless steel and acrylic. Founded by Shuzo Hamachi , Scapes stands out for its minimalist and conceptual aesthetic, pushing the boundaries between nature and design. Awarded at the 2025 London Design Awards , the brand continues to explore new dialogues between craftsmanship and modernity. At the event, Scapes will present its collaboration with CANON , ALBOS , to be released soon, as well as a collection of bonsai pots created in collaboration with HATAMAN TOUEN Co., Ltd.

# Explore Exhibition Booths

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/business-leaders-forum/business-summit-0611/explore-exhibition-stands.html
Nespresso , a brand under the Nestlé Group , specializes in capsule coffee and offers a wide range of premium blends sourced from exceptional coffee - growing regions. Combining innovation , design , and a strong commitment to sustainability , Nespresso delivers a high-end coffee experience both at home and in the workplace . The brand is also actively engaged in capsule recycling and responsible coffee sourcing .

French Bloom is a premium French alcohol-free sparkling wine brand that blends French savoir-faire with wellness. Created by Maggie Frerejean-Taittinger and Constance Jablonski , French Bloom uses organic grapes and natural ingredients to craft elegant, festive cuvées without compromise. It offers a refined alternative to traditional champagne, celebrating joy, health, and inclusivity in every glass.

Jean-Charles Rochoux is a renowned French master chocolatier known for his unique artisan creations. Based in Paris since 2004, he offers original ganaches , chocolate sculptures , and his famous Saturday Tablet , filled with seasonal fresh fruits. Combining tradition and creativity , he also opened a boutique in Tokyo, sharing his chocolate artistry with a touch of French elegance .

Suntory is a leading Japanese beverage company known for its commitment to quality and innovation . For this event, we are pleased to offer two of our signature products : Iyemon Green Tea , a refreshing and authentic Japanese tea , and Premium Boss Black , a rich , unsweetened coffee brewed for bold flavor .

Domaine Ricardelle de Lautrec is located in Coursan, Aude , at the crossroads of La Clape, Minervois and Corbières . The Via Domitia , the ancient Roman road linking Rome to Spain, crosses our 50 hectares of vineyards . Once owned by the Toulouse-Lautrec family , the estate and its 19th-century cellars embody a rich heritage. For over 25 years , we have pursued our passion guided by the principles of biodynamic viticulture .

# Explore Exhibition Booths

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/business-leaders-forum/business-summit-0611/explore-exhibition-stands.html
KOMA is a furniture atelier founded in 2003 by Shigeki Matsuoka . With the concept of “creating products that embody the beauty of one-of-a-kind works” , the small workshop of about twenty artisans, located in the suburbs of Tokyo, is dedicated to handcrafting furniture that its makers believe represents the very best. These pieces are sold through its directly operated stores in Ogikubo (Suginami Ward) and Aoyama (Minato Ward) .

The company has received numerous prestigious design awards from around the world and continues to share the excellence of Japanese craftsmanship on the global stage.

CHIE IMAI’s MORRIS is a premium Japanese imo shōchū crafted in Kagoshima from Golden Sengan sweet potatoes and black kōji . Inspired by French elegance and the idea of "drinking perfume," it offers a smooth, floral, and refined flavor at 25% ABV . Awarded Double Gold at the 2023 San Francisco World Spirits Competition and International Spirits Challenge, it’s a sophisticated choice even for those new to shōchū.

# TV Studio

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/business-leaders-forum/business-summit-0611/tv-studio.html
# TV Studio

As part of the annual Business Summit , the TV Studio returns for a new edition co-presented by the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan (CCIFJ) , in partnership with Nikkei and the French Embassy in Japan . This exclusive media platform gives participating companies and guests a unique opportunity to share their vision and insights in a 10-minute interview , reaching a high-level international business audience .

Interviews will be conducted by Régis Arnaud , Editor in Chief of France Japon Eco , a bilingual magazine under the CCIFJ since 2004. Based in Japan since 1995, he is also Japan-based correspondent for Le Figaro and Challenges and contributes regularly to Toyo Keizai . With over 25 years covering the Japanese economy and Franco-Japanese business relations , Régis brings deep expertise and valuable perspective.

Joining him is Yann Rousseau , Tokyo Bureau Chief for Les Échos . Having worked across Asia for nearly two decades —including in Beijing, Hanoi, Phnom Penh, and Paris —he settled in Tokyo in 2011. Yann is widely recognized for his sharp analysis of Japan’s economy and society . He co-authored the investigative book Le Fugitif (2020) with Régis Arnaud, exploring the Carlos Ghosn affair , and frequently comments on Japanese affairs in French-language media and podcasts.

Together, Régis and Yann offer insightful and authoritative interviews . Their extensive experience and credibility make this year’s TV Studio a can’t-miss opportunity for anyone aiming to boost their profile and impact in the international business community .

This year’s TV Studio is designed in collaboration with Koma , known for its refined furniture craftsmanship , and Scapes , which provides elegant bonsai arrangements that bring a touch of Japanese aesthetics to the set creating a sophisticated and harmonious atmosphere befitting this prestigious event.

We offer support structured in two complementary phases, enabling you to move from initial market validation to the development of concrete commercial opportunities.

Each mission is led by a local team of experienced consultants who act as true representatives of your company in Japan.

## Specificities of the Japanese Market

- In Japan, business discussions and decision-making processes are generally gradual and built on relationships of trust. Initial meetings are typically arranged only once a genuine level of interest has been confirmed (on average, 10% of prospects contacted), ensuring a high level of qualification among the contacts met during the mission.

- Between the initial contact and the signing of a contract, business agreements generally require a longer timeframe, often ranging from 1 to 3 years, depending on the industry and the organizational complexity of the companies involved.

- In this context, the objective of this mission is not to secure immediate contracts, but rather to build relationships of trust, validate market interest, and establish a structured sales pipeline designed to support sustainable business development in Japan.

## CCIFJ helps you prepare and optimize your participation in trade shows in Japan

Trade shows are important occasions to showcase your products and/or services. Are you looking to optimize your participation?

Relying on our network, our experts will organize everything you need to participate. We can also accompany or represent you at a trade show that you simply wish to visit.

Description of the service

We can assist you before and throughout the duration of the trade show:

- Logistics and administration: Managing and monitoring your registration process with the organizers (negotiating the location, price, and area, setting up your booth). Assisting the import procedures for the products to be exhibited. Preparing the brand presentation documents (in the local language if necessary).

- Communication and promotion: Social media marketing and implementation of a promotional campaign targeting your potential clients.

- Support for business development: Training session on conducting business in Japan.

- On-site support: Interpreting services for welcoming clients and managing contacts on-site. Possibility of organizing a B2B meeting program for you.

The CCIFJ offers to domicile your V.I.E employee in its office and take care of salary and administrative procedures (payroll, taxes, and visa).

The V.I.E formula allows you to:

- Control your budget: Social security exemptions in France, possibility of financing your V.I.E.

- Delegate administrative management to Business France.

- Have a flexible HR solution: Transfers from one country to another, contract duration of 6 to 24 months - you define the mission that suits your needs.

Expenses related to employing a V.I.E often benefit from national and regional subsidies , such as import-export credits, Bpifrance export development loans, and substantial subsidies covering a significant portion of the V.I.E's cost in many French regions.

## A key driver of direct savings for your business

Companies established outside France can recover VAT on a wide range of operational and event-related expenses:

- Trade shows, conferences, and seminars: Registration fees, booth rental, room rental, and admission fees

- Event organization and production: Furniture rental or purchase, booth decoration, floral arrangements, electricity, telecommunications, as well as hostesses/reception staff and professional interpreters

- Catering and hospitality: Business meals at restaurants, catering services, food, and beverages

- Intangible and professional services: Marketing, advertising campaigns, legal advisory, and IT services

- Logistics and fleet: Commercial vehicle rental, freight and transport of goods or machinery, and fuel expenses (including up to 80% refundable VAT on diesel)

Foreign companies or organizations established outside the EU that incur expenses in France can benefit from this service. Please note: the company applying for this service must not be registered for French VAT

French VAT reclaim procedures are technical, and administrative requirements regarding supporting documentation are strict. CCI France Japon handles the entire recovery process on your behalf:

- In-depth verification of your company’s eligibility

- Full preparation and filing of the official refund application

- Direct representation and liaison with the French tax authorities

- End-to-end monitoring until the actual disbursement of funds

# Why expanding into Japan?

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/commercial-support/why-expanding-into-japan.html
# Why expanding into Japan?

CHECK OUR NEWS SECTION

Japan: The Third-largest Economy in the World

Renowned for its advanced technologies, unique culture, and capacity of resilience, Japan attracts many international companies. It's a country projected towards the future, modern, and yet deeply traditional. Ready to embrace innovations from abroad but less inclined to integrate foreign influences. Its corporate culture, strongly influenced by a diversity of historical and cultural factors, often creates barriers to the establishment of economic partnerships. Nevertheless, in recent years, commercial ties between Japan and other countries have significantly developed.

With a GDP of 3.7 trillion euros in 2022 (1.1% growth), Japan emerges as the country with the third largest economy in the world. It is also one of the world's largest importers and serves as the gateway for businesses to enter the North Asian market.

As the eleventh most densely populated country in the world, with over 124 million inhabitants within 377,975 square kilometers (329 people per square kilometer), the majority of its population is concentrated in the capital, Tokyo, and other major Japanese cities such as Nagoya, Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe, and Hiroshima.

Tokyo: The World's Largest Economic Megalopolis

In 2023, the Tokyo metropolitan area has a population of 37 million inhabitants with a very high density (5,000 people per square kilometer). Commercial zones, numerous and diverse, are mainly organized around train stations. They are interconnected by a sophisticated and efficient transportation network. Services, finance, and insurance are the dominant sectors in the Japanese capital.

Regional Japan

13 Japanese cities have a population of over one million inhabitants and the country's population is 91% urban. Each region has its own strengths: the north specializes in agri-food industries, woodworking, and paper; the region surrounding Nagoya, Chubu, hosts major automotive and aerospace industrial sites. Osaka is renowned for electronics, and Fukuoka in the south of the country is known for its connections with Asia.

Japanese Consumers

# Why expanding into Japan?

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/commercial-support/why-expanding-into-japan.html
Japanese Consumers

With an average monthly salary of 2,120 euros in 2022, the Japanese population enjoys one of the highest purchasing powers in the world and a relatively low unemployment rate (2.6% in 2022). Its high standards and strong attraction to novelty and trend set it apart. Japan often serves as a preferred test market for the global launch of new products or services. French, in particular, maintains a high reputation in areas such as cosmetics, luxury goods, gastronomy, and fashion. The Japanese market is also the world's third-largest e-commerce market.

Japan, global leader in innovation

Japan is the country that allocates the highest proportion of its GDP to R&D (3.4% of GDP compared to 2.2% in France) and is the second-largest filer of patents in the world. The country's R&D accounts for 20% of global R&D. Recognized as a technological leader in B2C, Japan also excels in many B2B sectors. It has 5,328 researchers per million inhabitants (compared to 4,205 in the United States and 4,233 in France).

Economic Trends

As the third-largest global economic power and a member of ASEAN, Japan is deeply integrated into Asia. In 2022, it is China's second-largest supplier, with 57% of its exports directed towards Asia, a share that has been increasing since the 2000s. Japan's integration into Asian economies is a key factor in the country's current success, benefiting from the growth of emerging Asian countries.

The quality of Japanese products, their constant renewal, and the unparalleled focus on customer's experience are strengths that allow certain Japanese conglomerates to remain among the most profitable and powerful groups in the world. Furthermore, Japan has secured mastery of key technologies in many high-tech sectors.

# Why expanding into Japan?

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/commercial-support/why-expanding-into-japan.html
According to the Economic Complexity Observatory, Japan has the world's most "complex" economy. This means that it exports a wide variety of highly sophisticated and unique products. The country has maintained the top position in this ranking since the 1990s, thanks to the quantity and quality of its expertise and its strong economic relations. Its major exports include vehicles, integrated circuits, vehicle accessories and components, machinery, and photographic equipment.

Demographically, the declining population and increasing life expectancy create new market segments. Seniors receive special attention, whether they are active or retired. This segment of society has high purchasing power and demands specific treatment in terms of leisure, services, and well-being. Japan has thus become a laboratory for new trends that most Western societies will face soon with the aging of their populations.

On the financial front, Japan remains a crucial player. With the strength of its external trade, the country holds the world's second-largest foreign exchange reserves (USD 1.265 trillion as of April 2023) and remains one of the major funders globally.

In 2011, the Fukushima incident raised questions about the energy mix, particularly the role of nuclear power. Japan still has operational reactors that function very sporadically. Before the incident, nuclear power accounted for 29% of the country's electricity supply, a gap that the country now needs to fill through imports, which weighs on the traditionally surplus trade balance. However, this situation acts as a driving force for energy transition in Japan and has prompted the country to set ambitious targets for renewable energy use.

Following the decisions of former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, Japan embarked on a series of deep reforms known as "Abenomics" since 2013. The government aims to: 1) stimulate domestic demand through massive public spending (EUR 671 billion in 2014), 2) inject liquidity into the economy to encourage lending and investment, and 3) liberalize certain key sectors (such as the pharmaceutical industry and energy).

Trade Relations between France and Japan

Nearly 10,000 French companies exported a total of 6.5 billion euros to Japan in 2021, a 15.6% increase compared to their level in 2020 (5.6 billion euros).

The volume of French exports has not yet returned to the exceptional level of 2019 (7.7 billion euros, partly due to the implementation of the EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) in February 2019); however, it is returning to the average observed during the 2014-2018 period. The trade deficit against France amounted to -2.9 billion euros in 2021.

The aerospace sector (1.5 billion euros in 2021, 23% of total exports; +116%) is a significant driver of French exports to Japan.

The agri-food sector maintains a good level, and Japan remains our top customer in this segment in Asia. French exports increased by 6% in 2021 (1.23 billion euros, 19% of total exports), close to the record level of 2019 (1.31 billion euros). Half of French agri-food exports to Japan consist of wines and spirits.

Luxury products, textiles, clothing, as well as chemicals, perfumes, and cosmetics accounted for over 22% of French exports to Japan in 2021, with respective increases of 7% and 5.3%.

Regarding energy, France has a very small market share in this sector in Japan (1%) because it primarily exported nuclear industry-related technologies, which have been stagnant in the archipelago in recent years. The Japanese government is now investing billions of euros in renewable and green energies, mainly hydrogen but also wind, solar, and ammonia.

# Why expanding into Japan?

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/commercial-support/why-expanding-into-japan.html
In 2021, Japan is France's 13th largest customer, its 12th largest supplier, and its 2nd largest Asian trading partner after China, for both imports and exports.

In 2020, France was the 3rd largest foreign investor in Japan, behind the United States and Singapore. France has 500 companies in Japan, with 69% belonging to the manufacturing sector (Air France, Michelin, Renault, Valeo, Air Liquide, Total, Sanofi Aventis, Danone...) and 31% belonging to the services sector (Axa, BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, JCDecaux, Orange...).

# Hello Tomorrow Japan

Since 2017, Hello Tomorrow Japan has been energizing local innovation communities in Japan, marking a significant impact on the country's deep tech landscape.

Hello Tomorrow Japan is part of the global Hello Tomorrow network, a global network born in France in 2011, which promotes and supports cutting-edge innovations, bridging the gap between ideas and their concrete implementation. Focused on deep tech, Hello Tomorrow helps startup founders generate meaningful change and tackle complex global challenges through collaboration and entrepreneurship.

Deep tech refers to cutting-edge technologies rooted in scientific discoveries or technical innovations, capable of delivering significant breakthroughs and disrupting various industry sectors.

Our core mission in Japan is to bridge the gaps in local and global ecosystems by connecting innovators, industry leaders and investment opportunities. Through events and networking, we address the specific needs and interests of Japan's innovation community and facilitate knowledge sharing, idea exchanges and meetings to create meaningful connections and partnerships that foster innovation.

# BONJOUR FRANCE

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/discover-our-events/bonjour-france.html
# BONJOUR FRANCE

Each year, BONJOUR FRANCE hosts, with its French and Japanese partners, exceptional events that highlight the French " Art de vivre ".

To truly grasp what constitutes the French " Art de vivre " is not an easy task. Living “ à la française” means taking time to have a nice meal, to learn, to dream, to share…

Throughout the year, BONJOUR FRANCE invites the Japanese public to discover the French way of life, by sharing French traditional expertise in a variety of modern and innovative ways.

BONJOUR FRANCE proposes to share unique cultural moments, to discover our gastronomy in an informal manner, to taste new products that cannot be found in Japan and to take part in unique lifestyle events in the mythical department stores and other places.

Find more about BONJOUR FRANCE program on https://bonjourfranceccifj.com/ and come take part in our numerous events to discover the French way of life.

France has dressed up for the occasion, come and meet her!

# French Business Awards

The French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan is pleased to present the 2027 edition of the French Business Awards, the awards ceremony that honors companies during our annual New Year’s networking event.

For this 16th edition , the winners—carefully selected by the jury—will receive an award recognizing their excellence, uniqueness, and commitment in areas ranging from innovation to their dedication to sustainable development.

An award will also be presented to the company that, during the 2025–2026 period, has distinguished itself through organizational excellence and remarkable results.

Beyond the awards ceremony, the French Business Awards is above all a convivial and unifying event . Bringing together around 100 guests for a warm and engaging evening, it also offers a great opportunity to expand networks and foster connections within the business community.

Applications will be closed December 15th 2026.

The award ceremony will be held on January 28th 2027 in Tokyo.

## About the awards :

Any company, whether French or Japanese, operating in Japan may submit an application for one of our awards, with a limit of one application per company. To highlight the diversity of our members and their various fields of activity, we encourage every company to apply in one of the categories.

※ Depending on the awards, being a member a member of the Chamber, might be mandatory for candidacy.

## Company of the Year Award - 2027

The French Business Awards’ Company of the Year Award recognizes a company or SME that has stood out for its excellence, dynamism, and the quality of its achievements within the 2025–2026 fiscal year.

This award recognizes an organization which, in every way, demonstrates outstanding performance, innovation, and success, and which fully embodies the values of an inspiring and ambitious company.

## Credit Agricole CIB Japan Sustainability Award - 2027

The Credit Agricole CIB Japan Sustainability Award recognizes companies that place sustainability and positive impact at the heart of their strategy and growth.

This award recognizes a company or SME doing business with France and/or Japan that has committed to making a tangible contribution to a more sustainable future in Japan by 2025 and/or 2026.

Initiatives will be evaluated based on their impact on the market, the strength of their sustainable growth strategy, and their capacity for innovation.

APPLY

## Product/Service of the Year - 2027

The French Business Awards’ Product/Service of the Year Award recognizes a company or small business whose innovative product or service has successfully broken into the Japanese market over the past two years.

The jury will recognize an innovation for its uniqueness, impact, and potential, as well as for the company’s ability to continue innovating and expanding its horizons.

APPLY

## French Tech Tokyo - 2027

The French Tech Tokyo Award, recognizes a young company or startup, whether French or Japanese, that stands out for its ambition, innovation, and potential in the field of new technologies.

This award aims to highlight the talent that is contributing to the emergence of the next generation of technology leaders in Japan, while helping them expand their vision beyond borders and into new markets.

The jury will focus on evaluating the project’s growth potential, originality, and ability to transform innovation into a genuine opportunity for development.

The French Tech Tokyo Award is intended to recognize a startup focusing on the development of new technologies that was created within the last five years. This award recognizes exceptional growth potential, great originality in the projects undertaken, the ability to propose innovative and visionary ideas, and a strong ambition to break into and expand into new markets.

Eligible startups must have been registered in Japan since January 1, 2022, at the earliest. A bonus may be awarded to startups that wish to expand their operations into the French market or that already have links with France.

To apply for this award, please fill in this form in English (unless stated otherwise) as accurately and completely as possible.

French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan membership is not mandatory to apply for this category.

APPLY

The following information will be required to complete the application form: - Basic information about your company - A summary of its main activities - The company’s short- and long-term projects, as well as its development strategy - The company’s growth and financial performance in Japan - The reasons why you believe your company deserves to win this award (in detail).

# Galas

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/discover-our-events/galas.html
# Galas

Every year since 1978, the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Japan has had the pleasure to entertain its members, partners and clients with its exclusive gala evenings.

Those prestigious events are a showcase of the best of France in Japan, gathering almost 800 people in Tokyo, 300 in Kansai, 250 in Fukuoka and 150 in Nagoya, who are Japanese CEOs, politicians, celebrities or journalists.

The evening revolves around three key moments: first, a French Michelin-starred chef serves a special menu designed for the occasion; then, guests are treated to an exclusive show highlighting a famous aspect of French culture (with prestigious performers such as Julien Clerc, Sylvie Vartan); and finally, a giant raffle gives participants a chance to win numerous prizes from the biggest French brands, including travels to France, luxury accessories and cosmetics.

## The different editions

## Gala Tokyo

Every year since 1978, the biggest Gala of CCI France Japon gathers more than 800 guests in a prestigious hotel of Japan’s capital city.

## Gala Kansai

First Gala of CCI France Japon to be held outside of Tokyo, the Kansai Gala takes place every year in one of the main cities of the Kansai region (Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe), gathering more than 250 participants.

## Gala Fukuoka

Fukuoka, the dynamic city in the south of Japan, hosts the second gala outside Kanto of CCI France Japon, gathering more than 200 participants.

## Gala Nagoya

Nagoya, the industrial city in Japan, hosts the third gala outside Kanto of CCI France Japon.

# Gala Tokyo

Since 1978, Gala Tokyo has been celebrating French gastronomy, culture and lifestyle . More than 800 guests get together every year in one of Tokyo’s finest hotels to discover the cuisine of a great French chef and the live performance of an artist. The evening wraps up with a giant raffle awarding prizes from the biggest French brands.

A must-go event for the French-Japanese community!

## Concepts

The CCI France Japon offers guests a three-part programme:

- A Michelin-starred French chef prepares a special menu created exclusively for the occasion.

- An exclusive show introduces guests to a different facet of French culture, featuring prestigious guests such as Julien Clerc and Sylvie Vartan.

- A grand raffle gives attendees the chance to win numerous prizes offered by leading French brands, including trips to France, luxury accessories, and cosmetic products.

Our gala evenings are ideal opportunities to invite business partners. They are also a chance to expand your Franco-Japanese network and promote your company!

# L'Espace@CCIFJ

## L'espace@CCIFJ

Looking for a unique place to host your next event? CCI France Japon is providing its members with a beautiful 120m² space that reconciles prestige, conviviality and practicality.

Located on the ground floor of the new premises of CCI France Japon, L’Espace@CCIFJ is designed to host all kind of events: conferences, trainings, industry events, networking, cocktails, product launches, concept store… L’Espace@CCIFJ is way more than a meeting room: it has direct access to the outside, full-height windows and a stylish design. Those unique elements add a ‘French touch’ that will give your events an exclusive twist.

Our event space is ideally situated at a short 2 min walk from the Hanzomon & Ginza lines, 5 min walk from Tokyo station and 10 min walk from the Imperial Palace. It is at the centre of Nihonbashi historical district, a unique mix of culture, commerce and history for more than 400 years in Tokyo. Recent developments have strengthened the position of Nihonbashi as a premium location for high-class business and shopping in Tokyo, a place your clients and collaborators will enjoy discovering, be they Japanese or from abroad.

## Testimonies

# Ema OKAMOTO Nishijin Okamoto Okamoto Orimono Co., Ltd Executive Managing Director

Originally from the northern region of Sapporo, Ema Okamoto specialized in textile design before joining the century-old workshops of Okamoto Orimono, founded by her husband’s great-grandfather. She began her career as head of design before taking on leadership roles within the company, established in 1909 and specialized in the weaving of luxurious “kinran” silk textiles for temples and shrines across Japan.

Despite the challenges posed by the decline of traditional weaving looms, rising raw material costs, and decreasing domestic demand, Okamoto Orimono continues to refine its techniques and pursue new collaborations in order to connect tradition with the future of weaving. Combining technical mastery and the exceptional quality of silk with the exploration of new patterns inspired by distant cultures and aesthetics, Ema Okamoto now works to bring this weaving art into the worlds of luxury architecture and interior design, both in Japan and internationally.

# Toma YAMAZOE Political figure and former mayor of Yosano

After studying architecture at the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture de Paris-Malaquais, Toma Yamazoe pursued further studies in metaphysics under Professor Frédéric Nef at the École des Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales (EHESS). During his time in France, he also worked as an interpreter for exhibitions in Paris and Brussels dedicated to the silk craftsmanship of the Tango region, particularly chirimen textiles.

Upon returning to Japan in 2009, he joined the Ozaki Yukio Memorial Foundation, dedicated to the promotion of democracy, and participated in its Gadō-juku program before being elected with the highest number of votes to the Yosano Town Council in 2010. In 2014, at the age of 32, he was appointed Mayor of Yosano, becoming the youngest mayor in Japan; a position he held for 12 years across three consecutive terms. He also served as the second president of the National Association of Young Mayors of Towns and Villages in Japan.

After the most intense crisis the world has faced since 2008, it is time for institutions and countries to adapt and reform again in light of the underlying issues the world is facing that the covid crisis has highlighted. As Japan strives toward a new form of capitalism that is more conscious of these new issues, there is much to learn from the its industrial model’s strengths and from how it is trying to overcome its shortcomings. By focusing on how Japan can concentrate on its core values as a nation of innovation and technology but also a nation of creativity and culture, we can start to grasp what the rest of the world can learn from this model to move towards a more sustainable future that respects both the planet and its workers.

To attempt address these issues, the 2022 French-Japanese Business Summit will gather top-level international speakers from diverse backgrounds – from institutions, citizens and businesses to social sciences, art and architecture – to share their visions, their strategies, and the opportunities they foresee.

HR BREAKFAST 2026 JAPAN SALARY SURVEY RESULTS: WHAT'S REALLY DRIVING HIRING, RETENTION AND CHANGE?

Date : October 8, 2025 (Wed) | Time : 9 AM - 11 AM

EVENT OVERVIEW

In this session, Dr. David Sweet, Managing Director of FocusCore Japan, will present highlights from the 2026 Salary Survey offering essential insights for leaders navigating Japan’s uniquely complex and shifting talent market.

Over the past year, Japan’s labor landscape has continued to evolve rapidly. While foreign firms face pressure from global market shifts, many are doubling down in Japan, capitalizing on the weak yen and stable workforce. But salary expectations, working styles, and employee values have changed—and companies must adapt.

This talk will cover:

- Current compensation trends

- Salary and bonus shifts

- Team growth and restructuring trends

- Top motivators

- What professionals value most (spoiler: it’s not money)

- How AI is expected to reshape different functions

- Upskilling & career investment trends

- Q&A

This session will be interactive and conclude with a few recommendations for companies navigating Japan’s complex hiring landscape in 2026.

GUEST-SPEAKER

Dr. David Sweet – Expert in Recruitment, Leadership, and Strategy

For the past 30 years, Dr. Sweet has specialized in HR and executive development, recruiting, and leadership development for top-tier companies across Asia. He is the Founder and CEO of FocusCore Group, a leading executive search consultancy, where he helps businesses identify and secure top talent.

He is also the author of six books、 including Sweet Sales , Sweet Success , and Recruit! Becoming the Top-Biller , and has been featured in Facebook & LinkedIn 対応履歴書いらずのソーシャルメディア転職術 for his expertise in social networking for recruitment.

### Overview

In today’s multicultural and high-pressure workplace, inclusive leadership is no longer a “nice to have”. It is a strategic capability linked directly to retention, engagement, innovation, and team performance.

This session blends neuroscience with emotional intelligence to help leaders understand why inclusion matters for the brain, what gets in the way, and how to build practical habits that create psychologically safe, connected, and empowered teams.

Designed for people leaders and HR professionals, this training offers a refreshing, human-centered lens: simple brain-based strategies that can be implemented immediately to improve team culture, reduce friction, and strengthen collaboration across backgrounds, generations, and functions.

- Understand why inclusive leadership matters and how it drives performance.

- Learn how the brain scans for threat or reward through five key social drivers.

- Apply three simple, brain-based habits that signal reward and strengthen connection.

The Ailes Rouges project ("Akai-Tsubasa") commemorates André Japy's Paris-Tokyo raid on a Caudron Simoun, which was cut short in 1936 by a crash near Mount Sefuri just 1,000 km from its destination, aiming to fly the restored aircraft along this final stretch to Tokyo. In 2026, events in France and Japan will mark the 90th anniversary of this flight and celebrate French-Japanese relations.

# Building Trust To Avoid Conflict or Burnout

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/building-trust-to-avoid-conflict-or-burnout.html
Build trust through everyday leadership, prevent conflict and burnout, and create stronger teams using proven Dale Carnegie principles.

## BUILDING TRUST TO AVOID CONFLICT OR BURNOUT

DATE: October 29, 2026 (Thu) | Time: 9AM - 12PM

Many workplace conflicts and cases of burnout are not caused by a lack of skill or motivation, but by a lack of trust. In this course, managers learn how to build trust through everyday interactions and address issues before they escalate.

The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, provide proven guidance for building relationships and managing emotions in today’s workplace.

By strengthening trust as the foundation of leadership, managers can prevent unnecessary conflict, protect their team’s energy, and create an environment that supports sustainable performance.

- Why conflict and burnout occur in the workplace

- How a manager’s words, attitudes, and behaviors impact trust

- Apply Dale Carnegie principles to building trust

- Address concerns through dialogue before they become serious problems

- Commit to incorporating trust-building behaviors into daily management

### TRAINER

Chizu SASAKI, Dale Carnegie

After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

# Cap Japon: 2h Pour acquérir les bons reflexes interculturels

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/cap-japon-2h-pour-acquerir-les-bons-reflexes-interculturels.html
En 2 heures, adoptez de bons réflexes interculturels pour comprendre les codes professionnels japonais et collaborer avec confiance dès votre arrivée.

## CAP JAPON 2H POUR ACQUERIR LES BONS REFLEXES INTERCULTURELS

Date : 4 Novembre, 2026 (Mer) | Heure : 17h - 19h JST

Langue : Français

Atelier interactif combinant apports ciblés, études de cas réels et mises en pratique.

### Vous préparez votre départ pour le Japon ou venez d’y arriver ?

Deux heures ne suffisent évidemment pas pour connaître toute la culture japonaise. Elles peuvent en revanche changer le regard avec lequel on aborde ses premières semaines au Japon.

Cette formation en ligne propose les repères interculturels essentiels pour mieux comprendre ce que l’on observe, éviter certaines interprétations trop rapides et adopter, dès le départ, les bons réflexes dans son environnement professionnel japonais.

Conçue comme une première boussole interculturelle , elle permet de mettre du sens derrière des comportements qui peuvent surprendre : importance du groupe, communication implicite, silence, consensus, rapport au temps, à la hiérarchie ou encore aux règles et aux processus.

L’objectif n’est pas d’apprendre « comment sont les Japonais », mais de changer de grille de lecture pour aborder le Japon avec davantage de justesse, de curiosité et de confiance.

### À qui s’adresse cette formation ?

Aux professionnels francophones :

- qui préparent leur départ pour le Japon ;

- qui viennent d’arriver au Japon ;

- ou qui commencent à travailler régulièrement avec des collègues ou partenaires japonais et souhaitent acquérir rapidement quelques clés de compréhension.

# Cap Japon: 2h Pour acquérir les bons reflexes interculturels

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/cap-japon-2h-pour-acquerir-les-bons-reflexes-interculturels.html
- ou qui commencent à travailler régulièrement avec des collègues ou partenaires japonais et souhaitent acquérir rapidement quelques clés de compréhension.

La formation est accessible aussi bien depuis la France que depuis le Japon , avec des horaires pensés pour permettre la participation depuis les deux pays.

### Objectifs de la formation

À l’issue de ces deux heures, les participants disposeront de premières clés pour :

- Regarder autrement certaines situations professionnelles rencontrées au Japon

- Comprendre quelques logiques culturelles fondamentales qui influencent les comportements au travail

- Mieux décoder la communication japonaise, notamment ce qui n’est pas toujours exprimé explicitement

- Eviter de juger trop rapidement un comportement à partir de ses propres références culturelles

- Commencer leur expérience japonaise avec des repères concrets pour communiquer et collaborer plus sereinement .

### Programme

1. Les clés essentielles pour comprendre la culture professionnelle japonaise

- Le groupe et l’individu

- Harmonie, consensus et importance du processus

- Quelques codes du monde professionnel japonais

2. Mieux communiquer et éviter les premiers malentendus

- Communication directe / indirecte

- Implicite, silence et non-dits

- Quelques réflexes concrets pour mieux collaborer

3. Échanges & questions

- Situations rencontrées ou anticipées par les participants

### FORMATRICE

Midori Maki Midori est consultante interculturelle spécialisée dans les relations France–Japon. Elle accompagne les entreprises dans l'amélioration de leur collaboration, en mettant l’accent sur la communication, la compréhension mutuelle et l’efficacité collective.

# Christmas Dinner at Meiji Kinenkan: A BONJOUR FRANCE Collaboration

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/diner-de-noel-au-meiji-kinenkan-une-collaboration-bonjour-france.html
Its history dates back to October 1881 (Meiji 14), when the Gokaishokujō, or “Banquet Hall,” was completed on the site of the present-day Akasaka Palace, which at the time served as a temporary imperial residence.

This hall hosted diplomatic receptions at which Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken received members of foreign royal families as well as dignitaries from around the world. It also served as the imperial dining hall and was used on numerous occasions for banquets and official meals.

In 1888 (Meiji 21), the building was also the setting for a decisive event in Japan’s constitutional history: in the presence of Emperor Meiji, the Privy Council held sessions there devoted to examining the draft Constitution of the Empire of Japan. This place is therefore closely linked to the birth of Japan as a modern constitutional state.

The building also bears witness to Empress Shōken’s determination to promote the modernization of the country and the adoption of Western clothing. In August 1886 (Meiji 19), the Empress herself wore a Western-style dress and received foreign guests at this location for the first time in such attire.

Through this initiative, she notably wished to encourage the development of domestic industries through the Westernization of clothing. Her resolve, summed up in these words: “If it can serve the country, I will do anything,” inspired women of the upper classes and contributed to the spread of Western fashion in Japan.

This change in clothing also had consequences for the interior design of the hall. In order to meet the requirements of diplomatic receptions and facilitate the wearing of Western-style dresses, the floor, initially covered with carpets, was subsequently renovated and fitted with geometrically patterned parquet flooring, made using the Japanese yosegi-bari technique.

# Christmas Dinner at Meiji Kinenkan: A BONJOUR FRANCE Collaboration

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/diner-de-noel-au-meiji-kinenkan-une-collaboration-bonjour-france.html
Subsequently, the building was bestowed upon Itō Hirobumi, a major figure in the drafting of the Constitution. In 1918 (Taishō 7), it was relocated to its present location in a section of the outer gardens of Meiji Jingu Shrine and was given the name Kempō Kinenkan, or “Constitution Memorial Hall.”

After hosting numerous events of national and social importance, it opened its doors on November 1, 1947 (Shōwa 22), under the name Meiji Kinenkan, as a reception venue for Meiji Jingu. In 2020 (Reiwa 2), its main building was officially designated a Tangible Cultural Property by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government.

Emperor Meiji laid the foundations of modern Japan, while Empress Shōken devoted her efforts to the development of culture, women’s education, and charitable activities. Her humanitarian commitment is notably embodied in the Empress Shōken Fund, established in support of the activities of the Red Cross and considered the oldest international humanitarian fund of its kind in the world.

Even today, the main building of Meiji Kinenkan perpetuates the memory of Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken. It continues to convey to present generations the spirit of their era, their commitment to serving the country, and the momentum that accompanied the birth of modern Japan.

In 2000, at the recommendation of the head chef of La Tour d’Argent, Olivier came to Japan as a cooking instructor for Le Cordon Bleu. After a year working as a technical director and executive chef at the Kobe and Tokyo branches of Le Cordon Bleu, he opened Chez Olivier in Ichigaya in 2009. Olivier considers himself to be both a chef and restaurateur. Thus, to provide the best possible dining experience for everyone, everyday at his restaurant, Olivier is involved not only in the kitchen, but also in the selection of wines and in the service.

Chez Olivier

The restaurant Chez Olivier, which in French means the “House of Olivier,” was opened in 2009 by chef-owner, Olivier Oddos, for guests to enjoy typical French in a relaxed atmosphere. The restaurant uses only the finest ingredients. The vegetables, most of which are organic, come from small growers all over Japan. Because Chef Olivier believes authentic tastes are essential, he is careful to make everything home-made. Nothing is made ahead of time. After an order is placed, Olivier and his staff will prepare the dishes. Olivier wants his guests to taste the flavors of the season, not only on special occasions, but everyday—just as naturally as breathing fresh air. So each day, the dishes at Chez Olivier take full advantage of what the seasons have to offer.

## EMPOWERING THROUGH WORDS: MASTERING CONSTRUCTIVE FEEDBACK

DATE: June 18, 2026 (Thu) | Time: 9AM - 12PM

Feedback is not about evaluating performance - it is a powerful way to develop people and unlock their potential. In this course, managers and leaders learn how to deliver constructive feedback that encourages ownership, strengthens trust, and supports continuous growth.

The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, are applied directly to feedback conversations in today’s workplace.

Through value-centered dialogue and practical approaches, participants learn how to give feedback that builds relationships while driving improvement.

### What You Will Learn

- Why feedback feels difficult

- How to reduce defensiveness in feedback conversations

- Apply Dale Carnegie principles to feedback

- Engage in dialogue that surfaces and connects with others’ values

- Commit to practicing feedback skills immediately in the workplace

After graduating from university, Chizu began her career at a travel agency, where she was involved in planning and proposing educational programs aimed at developing global talent. Through consulting sales work with clients from diverse cultural backgrounds, she developed a strong appreciation for the importance of cultivating internationally minded professionals.

She later joined a U.S. higher education institution, where she was responsible for public relations and educational outreach to promote global learning among students from around the world. During this time, she encountered Dale Carnegie Training through an internal staff development program and deeply resonated with its values and practical approach.

Since joining Dale Carnegie in 2017, Chizu has been designing and delivering customized corporate training programs tailored to clients’ specific needs. Her work focuses on supporting the growth of business professionals and driving organizational development.

# How to manage Millennials and GenZ

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/how-to-manage-millennials-and-genz.html
- Context of this program

Around 30% of new grads will quit their job within 3 years. 75% of millennials/Gen Z will prioritise the social impact of a company over the financial conditions offered to them when choosing a job. How they are valued as individuals is extremely important to them, but so is their privacy. Their definition of who to recognise as a superior is different, and should you not satisfy their communication expectations, total withdrawal can be as sudden as it can be absolute.

To us non-millennials/Gen Z individuals navigating the communications with our younger team members can be a source of stress and confusion as their expectations can come across as inconsistent. One is never sure what or when the next « […]harassment » will be coined and what one might be accused of. Non-compliance with requests, incomplete or off topic delivery of requested work, sudden disappearance (resignation) are factors that are not as rare as one would like them to be.

This course provides guidelines to help you understand how and what to communicate to help them maximise their potential, overcome their issues, and deliver the results you need them to deliver.

The Framework will also help you communicate with your younger team members in such a way as to make them feel comfortable and intrinsically motivated to complete the tasks you want to allocate to them.

- Who should attend?

If you are managing a team of people under 35, are finding it difficult to communicate with, and intrinsically motivate them, this is the course for you. If you have issues with employee retention, team efficiency, this course will provide you with a framework to overcome the issues and improve your team efficiency.

- Training program and objectives

This training has a strong group work and role play component. It is based on the belief you have to think it and experience it to keep it.

The training will be in 2 parts

Part I : About millennials and Gen Z

- A working definition of who they are.

- A description of their cultural background and, how it differs from hours

- Learning how their cultural background impacts their vision of the world and the way they communicate.

## Special guest

Françoise MORÉCHAND

- A Bridge Between Japan and France -

Françoise MORÉCHAND is a French lifestyle advisor and essayist, notably known for having served as beauty director at Chanel. She is currently an international advisor to the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art, Kanazawa. She is married to French music and film critic Tatsuji Nagataki.

Originally destined to become an interpreter in Chinese or Russian, she chose instead to devote herself to Japanese, convinced of Japan’s future potential. She studied at the École des langues orientales de Paris as well as at the Sorbonne, then settled in Japan in 1958 with her first husband. There, she taught French for Japan Airlines, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan, and Ochanomizu University.

She gained widespread recognition as the instructor on the NHK television program “French Conversation,” quickly becoming one of the best-known French women in Japan through her many appearances on television, radio, and in the press. After returning to France in 1964, she worked for Christian Dior and Revlon before returning to Japan in 1974 as beauty director of Chanel. She later continued her media activities, introducing French fashion, culture, and history to the Japanese public.

### Overview

Psychological safety is not simply about being “nice” or “easy to talk to.” It is a foundation for team performance, growth, and engagement.

In this course, managers learn how to act as Psychological Safety Champions—leaders who foster trust, encourage open dialogue, and empower team members to speak up, take risks, and learn from mistakes.

The program is grounded in the timeless principles found in How to Win Friends and Influence People and How to Stop Worrying and Start Living. These Dale Carnegie principles, practiced worldwide for over 100 years, are translated into practical approaches that fit today’s workplace and leadership challenges.

By creating an environment where people feel safe to contribute and grow, managers can build teams that achieve sustainable results and strong engagement.

- Understand what psychological safety is and why it directly impacts team performance

- Reflect on how a manager’s words, attitudes, and behaviors influence the team

- Learn trust-building communication based on Dale Carnegie principles

- Discover how to create an environment where ideas and concerns can be shared safely

- Identify clear, practical actions that can be applied immediately in the workplace

# Territory and community: Lessons in Leadership from the Maasaï

url: https://www.ccifj.or.jp/en/events/upcoming-events/event-details/event/territory-and-community-lessons-in-leadership-from-the-maasai.html
What can we learn from Kenya’s Maasaï and other traditional societies about being more relevant in what we do and who we are?

## HR BREAKFAST TERRITORY AND COMMUNITY LESSONS IN LEADERSHIP FROM THE MAASAÏ

Date : October 20, 2026 (Tue) | Time : 9:00am - 11:00am

Ask a Maasaï chief what matters most in his life and in his role as a leader, and two answers invariably come first: my territory and my community.

From there arise fundamental questions:

- What does the community need to survive, protect itself and thrive?

- What resources and tools does it need?

- What obstacles will it encounter along its journey?

- How should decisions be made, responsibilities shared and knowledge passed on?

Drawing on English explorer Anthony Willoughby ’s lifelong experience with traditional societies, and on his recent journey among the Maasaï with Tokyo based Executive Coach François-Xavier Lienhart , we invite you to an interactive and exploratory conversation about what traditional wisdom can teach us about leadership in today’s organizations and, in particular, in modern Japan.

Together, we will explore some fundamental dimensions of leadership: wisdom, strength and beauty; courage and protection; power and responsibility; decision-making; authority and seniority; symbols and rituals; tradition and modernity; transmission and culture; community and belonging.

Rather than offering ready-made answers, we shall use these perspectives to question some of our assumptions about leadership and organizational life.

- What makes us relevant as leaders?

- What gives meaning to our actions?

- What do the communities we lead actually need from us?

- And what should we preserve, change or pass on?

### Takeaways

Participants will have a unique opportunity to step outside their usual organizational frameworks and reflect on important aspects of their lives as leaders and members of a community. The discussion will encourage reflection on our own behaviours, the meaning of our actions, and the contribution we make to the organizations and communities to which we belong.

## "THE CULTURE MAP" A POWERFUL TOOL FOR UNDERSTANDING CULTURAL DIVERSITY AND GETTING THE BEST OUT OF IT FOR YOUR ORGANIZATION

Date : November 30, 2026 (Mon) | Time: 1:30PM - 5PM

Language: English

In today’s globalized workplace, business success depends on your ability to navigate cultural differences with accuracy and confidence.

This goes beyond language and beyond goodwill. Misunderstandings happen, and they can be costly.

Using INSEAD Professor Erin Meyer’s Culture Map, a field-tested model for decoding how cultural differences shape international work, this session helps you understand how and why people from other cultures think and act the way they do.

The focus goes beyond France and Japan, with insights that also include China, Korea, the US, and diverse European countries.

### What you will learn

- How cultural differences impact international work life, using the Culture Map framework

- How to combine a smart analytical model with practical, actionable advice

- How to learn through a mix of theoretical explanations, group work, and simulations

### Target Audience

- Expatriates recently assigned to a managerial position in Japan.

- Japanese executives working for a foreign owned company and who want to understand better how people think at the Head Office.

- Japanese employees working for a non-Japanese manager.

- Regional APAC leaders who need to grasp the cognitive and behavioral logic of their overseas colleagues or clients.

- Anyone curious about culture, with a strong desire to learn something new that will help them in their daily life at work and with friends.

## Membership categories:

Highest membership status for the members wishing to have a significant impact of the French-Japanese business community while showing their investment and support to the CCIFJ . This status grants exclusive services, maximum exposure and personalized solutions.

Annual membership fee: 650.000 yens

(From 1 st of January to 31 st of December)

STATUS BENEFITS

Start-up membership is an ideal choice for small and young companies that wish to develop their activities, take advantage of the CCI France Japon services and benefit from a dynamic business network and community. This status is reserved for companies with less than 3 years of existence, for the first two years of membership.

Annual membership fee: 140.000 yens

(From 1st of January to 31st of December) STATUS BENEFITS

Dedicated membership status for individual and independent professionals wishing to expand their business network. Individual members can participate in all events organized by the CCI France Japon. This status is reserved to freelancers, micro-structures or retired people.

Annual membership fee: 80.000 yens

(From 1st of January to 31st of December)

BENEFITS STATUS

Active membership is aimed to companies that are looking to increase their visibility, develop strong partnerships with the French-Japanese business community while being fully involved in all of the activities of the CCI France Japon.

Annual membership fee: 295.000 yens

(From 1st of January to 31st of December)

STATUS BENEFITS

Regional membership is an ideal choice for companies based in regional areas that do not have a branch in the Tokyo metropolis. CCI France Japon Kansai, Kyushu, Chubu, Gunma, and Fukui support your business and international expansion locally, in coordination with the Tokyo Chamber. This status is reserved for companies that do not have an office or permanent staff in the prefectures of Tokyo, Chiba, Saitama, or Kanagawa.

# Honorary committee

The CCI France Japon set up in January 2001 a "Franco-Japanese Strategic Committee". Renamed as "Honorary Committee" in 2007, as part of its rapprochement with the Japanese business community, it aims to strengthen economic and commercial relations between our two countries, dispensing advice and guidance on the development of the Franco-Japanese bilateral relationship. This Committee was relaunched in 2013 at the instigation of Hisataka Nobumoto, Vice-President of the CCI France Japon, with new high-ranking Japanese personalities.

FJE 183 : Sports : 3,2,1… Japon

Le Japon n’est pas seulement une puissance industrielle, culturelle, économique et financière : c’est aussi une puissance sportive . Arrivé troisième aux deux derniers Jeux olympiques, il s’impose dans de plus en plus de disciplines : non seulement base-ball et sumo mais désormais football, rugby, volleyball, basketball, escrime et d’autres.

Ces performances ont d’authentiques retombées. La construction d’infrastructures bat son plein. Les athlètes deviennent des objets de marketing. Les droits de diffusion des compétitions augmentent. Mais le sport au Japon n’est pas encore la locomotive économique qu’elle est devenue dans certains pays. L’hospitalité autour des compétitions en est à ses balbutiements, par exemple. Ces carences font du Japon un marché très prometteur pour des entrants étrangers. C’est pourquoi France Japon Eco fait le point sur le sport au Japon dans sa dernière édition.

Dans ce numéro également : le récit de la fusion Nikon Essilor racontée par Xavier Fontanet, son principal architecte ; un reportage et une analyse de l’ouverture (timide) du Japon à l’armement européen ; un compte-rendu des récents événements les plus marquants de la CCI. FJE 186 : Ressources humaines : comme vous nous manquez

Les ressources humaines sont devenues la première préoccupation des entreprises au Japon. Du directeur de filiale au plâtrier, de l’informaticien au serveur, tous les postes sont à pourvoir. Le Japon est entraîné dans une spirale de baisse démographique qui siphonne sa population active. L’« armée de réserve » de femmes et de personnes âgées ainsi que la main d’œuvre immigrée ont permis de ralentir ce phénomène depuis dix ans ; pas de l’endiguer, ni de le retourner. Les entreprises doivent désormais « organiser cette pénurie » de main-d’œuvre, qui s’impose progressivement à toutes les économies, proches (Taiwan, la Corée du Sud…) ou lointaine (Italie, France…)

Dans quels secteurs la pénurie est-elle la plus criante ? Comment le Japon s’adapte-t-il ? Pourquoi l’offre de ressources humaines, de moins en moins satisfaisante au vu de la demande, ne se traduit-elle pas par une hausse des salaires ? France Japon Eco répond à ces questions en interrogeant les acteurs de terrain.

FJE 184 : Rêves japonais

Chaque année, le Business Summit de la CCI France Japon est l’occasion de rencontrer quelques-uns des acteurs, étrangers et locaux, de l’économie et de la société japonaise. L’édition 2025 a une fois encore été riche en talents de toutes origines. Robotique, finance, sports, tech… Réformistes ou « gardiens de temple », tout le monde se retrouve au Business Summit. Nous reproduisons quelques-unes de leurs interventions les plus intéressantes.

Dans le 184, nous revenons aussi sur la TICAD, sommet Afrique-Japon dans laquelle la France a une place particulière. Nous faisons le point sur les conséquences du yen bas, et vous présentons Shuhei Abe, une des figures de la finance japonaise. La nouvelle génération de décideurs au Japon a aussi toujours sa place – dans la rubrique « La relève ». Nous racontons aussi le geste de Louis Schweitzer, figure-clé de la relation franco-japonaise, avec des anecdotes exclusives. Le Japon n’a pas été une étape mais un fil rouge de sa vie et de sa carrière, comme beaucoup de lecteurs de FJE.

Enfin le Japon accueille de plus en plus de chefs d’entreprise, curieux de prospecter davantage ce marché. Ils font très fréquemment escale à la CCI France Japon. Nous avons créé pour eux une nouvelle rubrique, qui renseigne le lecteur sur la place du Japon dans le monde.

France Japon Eco, le magazine bilingue de la vie des affaires au Japon, raconté par ses acteurs de terrain !

FJE 185 : yen, où vas-tu ?

Le sujet du yen a toujours occupé une place disproportionnée dans la vie des affaires au Japon. Ses mouvements en yo-yo obligent les entreprises (pour leurs coûts et leurs marges) et les particuliers (pour leurs achats de biens importés, pour leurs voyages à l’étranger…) à des arbitrages constants.

Mais depuis l’épidémie de COVID, la monnaie japonaise s’est durablement installée à un niveau historiquement bas. France Japon Eco a interrogé chefs d’entreprise et particuliers pour comprendre les effets de cette situation sur leurs activités, et s’il est souhaitable qu’elle cesse.

Aussi dans FJE : une interview exclusive de l’ambassadrice de France au Japon. Peu de temps après son arrivée, Béatrice le Fraper du Hellen a bien voulu nous recevoir quelques jours avant la visite du Président de la République Emmanuel Macron au Japon. Elle nous explique comment passer, selon son expression, d’un « partenariat d’exception » à un « partenariat exceptionnel », en profitant d’un nouveau coup de projecteur, cette fois politique, sur le Japon.

Toujours dans FJE : l’interview exclusive de Takuji Aida. L’un des économistes les plus influents du Japon expose la politique économique de la nouvelle Première ministre Sanae Takaichi. Une lecture essentielle pour comprendre la politique économique en train de se dessiner.

FJE vous explique aussi la réforme prochaine du shopping duty free dans ce maillon essentiel du secteur qu’est le Japon : un quart des ventes mondiales de duty free a lieu ici.

FJE 180 : Transformation énergétique rapport d’étape

Le Japon est sur le point de publier sa nouvelle feuille de route énergétique, qui pavera la voie vers son objectif « zéro CO 2 d’ici 2050, avec une importante étape en 2030. Grâce aux témoignages exclusifs des acteurs de terrain membres de la CCI France Japon et à leurs collaborateurs (entreprises externes, représentants des administrations concernées), FJE vous offre une analyse originale de l’état d’avancement des progrès sur ce dossier majeur, en le comparant notamment avec la situation française.

Aussi dans FJE 180 : les dessous de la reprise du réseau aéroportuaire du Kansai par Vinci Airports et son partenaire Orix à l’occasion des trente ans de l’aéroport KIX ; une analyse des défis de l’industrie logistique, si excellente jusqu’ici ; un reportage dans les rayons de Seibu Ikebukuro, grand magasin légendaire en pleine rénovation ; une brève histoire de l’innovation dans l’industrie pharmaceutique japonaise – et ses travers actuels. Enfin une analyse sur l’étrange absence de compte commun parmi la panoplie des services bancaires au Japon. Et l’actualité de la CCI France Japon bien sûr.

# National Travel Discount - Share your offer

Japan launched its new domestic travel subsidy program from Oct. 11 to late December as part of efforts to spur domestic tourism and revive the coronavirus-hit economy.

The "National Travel Discount" offers a 40% discount on travel costs, up to a maximum of 8,000 yen/person per night for a trip using public transportation (train/subway, bus, airplane, etc.) and 5,000 yen for a trip other than that (without using public transport or accommodation only), with local coupons that can be used at restaurants, souvenir shops, etc. worth 3,000 yen on weekdays and 1,000 yen on weekends.

The National Travel Discount program, which is available to Japan residents only, comes in the wake of the "Go To Travel" subsidy program and expands on similar existing programs operating at the prefectural level.

For the occasion, the CCI France Japon offers its members a way to communicate on their establishment, company or special offers with many options!

# 100 days to go to Rugby World Cup France 2023! Japan joins top ranked teams

The countdown is on to Rugby World Cup France 2023 with 31 May marking 100 days to go to the start of the tournament on September 8! This will be the 10th Rugby World Cup since the first tournament which was jointly hosted by New Zealand and Australia in 1987. This year also marks a milestone in the history of rugby with 200 years since the birth of the sport in 1823 when William Ellis of “Rugby School” in England first ran with the ball in his hand during a football game.

In the past, the Japanese national team suffered a devastating defeat of 145 - 17 at the third Rugby World Cup against the All Blacks, however at the tournament in 2015 the team's tenacious comeback to victory over the mighty South African team prompted head coach Eddie Jones to proclaim "The world has changed”. In addition, the team accomplished its elusive goal of finishing in the top eight at the last tournament in 2019.

Japan's national team has been steadily gaining international recognition and has been classified as a "Tier 2" nation, however the international governing body World Rugby (WR) has reorganized the framework of the 10 "Tier 1" nations to create a "High Performance Union" of 11 teams, including Japan. This is indeed very exciting news for Japan.

Current candidates for this tournament to keep an eye out for include veterans such as captain Atsushi Sakate and Michael Leitch, as well as youngsters like 22 year old Warner Dearns of New Zealand, who stands at over 2 meters tall and scored a spectacular try against the All Blacks last year. Others include another 22 year old, tough fly-half Seungsin Lee and 24 year old flanker Koji Shimokawa, who’s situational judgment is outstanding. The level of talent continues to grow with each game and expectations are high for the future and further growth of these young players.

# Discovering the craftsmanship of Aritaya, an artisan soy sauce brewer.

On 22 May 2026, the CCIFJ organised a company visit to Aritaya, a soy sauce brewer located in Gunma Prefecture.

On 22 May, the Gunma Office held its first event of the year. On this occasion, participants had the opportunity to visit Aritaya, a member company of the CCIFJ located in the city of Annaka.

The event began with a tour of Aritaya’s facilities in a warm and friendly atmosphere. Mr Yuasa Kohki, representing the seventh generation of the family business, introduced us to the company’s craftsmanship as well as one of its signature products: a naturally brewed soy sauce matured in the Usui Tunnel. This product perfectly reflects the company’s philosophy of developing unique flavours rooted in the local terroir, shaped by Annaka’s climate and distinctive micro-organisms.

The visit continued with a workshop organised by the Annaka Tourism Association, during which participants had the opportunity to press their own soy sauce in an atmosphere filled with curiosity and enthusiasm.

The event then concluded with a tasting session featuring dishes specially prepared for the occasion, carefully paired with two soy sauce specialities: firstly, koikuchi, brewed from whole soybeans and fermented in a single stage; secondly, saishikomi, which undergoes a double fermentation process.

We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Aritaya for their warm welcome and kindness throughout the day.

Many thanks as well to all the participants for their enthusiasm and cheerful spirit.

We look forward to seeing you again at future events in Gunma.

# A Memorable Sake Event in Collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo and Special Guest Sonia Bichet

On Saturday, June 15th, we had the pleasure of hosting an event in collaboration with Shimizu Seizaburo , a renowned sake brewery located in Suzuka, Mie Prefecture . We welcomed a special guest, Sonia Bichet , a MOF ( Meilleur Ouvrier de France ) Fishmonger, known for her exceptional skills at just 29 years old.

### Brewery Tour and Sake Tasting

The event started with an insightful tour of the brewery, allowing attendees to explore the production and bottling site of the celebrated Zaku sake bottles, notably winning the prestigious Kura Master competition in 2021 , among many other accolades.

Following the tour, we enjoyed a sake-tasting session, perfectly paired with delicious oysters from Mie provided by the MOF and Shimizu Seizaburo’s local partners. In a traditional toast inspired by the fishermen of Mie, we poured a bit of sake into an oyster shell, raised it to the sky, and said "Kanpai!" before savoring the delicious combination.

### Demonstration by Sonia Bichet

The highlight of the event was undoubtedly the demonstration by Sonia Bichet. Participants eagerly gathered around her table, where freshly shucked oysters were served. Throughout the event, Sonia's warmth and enthusiasm were evident as she passionately answered questions and shared her journey.

Sonia has been traveling the world (15 countries) for the past nine months, sharing her passion with younger generations and experiencing different fishing cultures. Despite the exhaustion from her extensive travels, including an incredible immersion with the Ama divers of Toba , Sonia's energy and charm quickly put everyone at ease. She not only showcases her often-stigmatized profession but also highlights the universal and borderless sharing of cuisine, enabling her to share her passion in any country.

### Conclusion
